items.followUp: Write down four differences between an atom and an ion.

rubric.why: Identifies the absence of an overall charge in a molecule.
rubric.description: A molecule is electrically neutral, unlike a molecular ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a molecule has no net charge.

rubric.why: Identifies the overall charge that distinguishes a molecular ion from a molecule.
rubric.description: A molecular ion has a net positive or negative charge, unlike a neutral molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a molecular ion has a net charge.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the two by their numbers of protons and electrons.
rubric.description: A molecule has equal numbers of protons and electrons; a molecular ion has unequal numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct proton/electron distinction for both.

rubric.why: Gives an example of each type to illustrate the distinction.
rubric.description: H2O or CO2 is a molecule; NH4+ or SO4^2- is a molecular ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct molecule example and one correct molecular-ion example.

modelAnswer: A molecule is a group of bonded atoms with no net charge; a molecular ion is a group of bonded atoms with a net charge.
A molecule is electrically neutral, whereas a molecular ion has a positive or negative charge.
A molecule has equal numbers of protons and electrons; a molecular ion has unequal numbers of protons and electrons.
Examples: H2O is a molecule, while NH4+ is a molecular ion.
